purpose: Plan 9 userland command and service compatibility matrix for Star 9 rc/shell workflows
rule: Commands are thin frontends over Star 9 namespaces, service files, task fds, device files, and 9P-style composition. They must not bypass the namespace/fd/device model.

commands.surface: star9-shell command, reachable from star9 rc external command dispatch
commands.notes: -c is accepted as a compatibility flag; namespace creation remains governed by Star 9 filesystem behavior.

commands.surface: star9-shell command, reachable from star9 rc external command dispatch
commands.implementation: ShellHost::unmount_path over star9-vfs::Namespace::unbind_path and ShellHost::unmount_binding over Namespace::unbind_source_path
commands.notes: The one-argument form removes the destination mountpoint. The two-argument form removes only bind layers whose recorded source path matches src, avoiding pointer-identity surprises for namespace self-binds.

commands.surface: star9-shell command, #srv and /srv service registry files, browser shell controller import services
commands.implementation: Runtime::register_loopback_service, Runtime::register_tcp_9p_service, ServiceRegistry, and browser import service registration
supported_forms: srv tcp!host!port name on native hosts
srv import!url#system name in browser shell
srv -m import!url#system name mountpoint in browser shell
evidence: Star9ShellController registers browser import services and mounts them through mount
commands.notes: Loopback Star 9 namespace exports are implemented by default. Native tcp!host!port registers a 9P client service through TcpStreamTransport when explicitly used. Browser raw TCP remains unavailable; browser services use import!/MessagePort now and should use WebSocket/WebTransport-shaped providers later.

commands.surface: star9-shell command over service registry and namespace binds
commands.notes: Service lookup accepts names plus srv/name or #srv/name forms. Auth/create flags are accepted where they do not change Star 9's local mount semantics.

Visible compatibility bind to #env for scripts expecting /env-style access.
Hidden service registry device. Entries are service descriptor files; remove unregisters a service.
